rationale: Evidence from iteration 6 (kd 0.9, the best raced design at 511.25): the oval held 20/20 finishes at 2.00 s with steering_oscillation 0.185, so the straights tolerate the extra damping. The s-bend reached 5/20 finishes with mean max_error 0.0608 m and steering_oscillation rising to 0.324, and the slalom had 0/20 finishes with max_error 0.066 m. Across kd 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 the s-bend max_error stayed at 0.060 to 0.061 m and s-bend finishes plateaued at 5/20 from kd 0.7 to 0.9. Speed (1.3, 1.1, 1.0) also left max_error flat, so the bend limit is not a speed effect. Interpretation: derivative action is still the most useful lever, but its gain per step is shrinking, and the rising s-bend oscillation shows that more kd also amplifies jitter. I follow the Evaluator's stated next step, a single change of kd from 0.9 to 1.0 with everything else fixed (base_speed 1.1, kp 1.6, ki 0, sensor_weights -2..2, last_direction, and the iteration 3 to 6 geometry unchanged). Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error edge below 0.06 m, with s-bend finishes at 6 to 8/20, a score of about 520 to 540, and the oval still at 20/20. Risks: s-bend steering_oscillation may rise above 0.35, and the oval may start losing finishes if kd is too high for the straights. Hypotheses to test next: (1) kd has reached its useful range, so the next gain must come from kp, since kp 1.4 may cut overshoot; (2) the flat max_error across speed and kd may point to the sensor layout (5 sensors at 0.03 m spacing, 12 mm footprint) limiting how early the robot sees a bend, which a sensor-size change could test later. Measurements wanted: per-track finish rate, max_error, steering_oscillation and completion_time, especially s-bend and slalom. If the oval loses finishes or s-bend oscillation exceeds about 0.4, return kd to 0.9 and test kp 1.4 next.
